intended_object: The dimension-shifting isomorphism Ext^q(X, Z^{n+1}) ≅ Ext^{q+1}(X, Z^n) for q > 0. It is the connecting map of the short exact sequence 0 → Z^n → R^n → Z^{n+1} → 0 of cycles of a resolution whose terms are Ext(X, –)-acyclic. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and its use in the naturality lemma.
explanation: `cyclesShortComplex n` is the sequence Z^n → R^n → Z^{n+1}, built from iCycles and toCycles; the library proves it is short exact. `covariantDimensionShift` is composition with the extension class of that sequence, i.e. the connecting map Ext^q(X, X₃) → Ext^{q+1}(X, X₁). It is shown to be bijective using Mathlib's covariant long-exact-sequence lemmas, which need Ext^q and Ext^{q+1} of the middle term to vanish. The hypothesis q > 0 is exactly what makes both groups vanish via `extAcyclic`, so the source and target degrees and the hypotheses match the standard dimension-shifting argument. The fully general version, for any short exact sequence with Ext-acyclic middle term, is the library's own `covariantDimensionShift`. This definition only specializes it to the cycle sequences of an acyclic resolution, which is the setting its content needs, so it is not too narrow. It is largely a proof step towards the comparison between Ext and the homology of the resolution, so `not_a_mathematical_object` would also be arguable. It is still a canonical, standard isomorphism and is correctly defined.
